prompt.en: After Abel's death, what did God say would happen to Cain's work as a farmer?

text.en: The soil would yield crops only in another land
He would trade his crops for Abel's flock
He would have to leave some fields unplanted
The soil would cease yielding well to him

explanation.en: God says the ground will not yield its strength to Cain and that Cain will become a wanderer.

prompt.en: Why did Abram question how God's promise would be fulfilled?

text.en: He believed Lot had been named his heir
He thought a son from Nahor would inherit
He expected a son born in Egypt to inherit
He was childless; his servant seemed to inherit

explanation.en: Abram says he is childless and names Eliezer of Damascus as the apparent heir; God replies that a son from Abram's own body will inherit.

prompt.en: What reason does Exodus give for the midwives disobeying Pharaoh's order about Hebrew baby boys?

text.en: They feared Pharaoh would punish their families
They feared God and kept the boys alive
They hoped the king would reward their service
They wanted Hebrew leaders to approve their work

explanation.en: The passage says the midwives feared God, did not follow Pharaoh's command, and saved the boys alive.

prompt.en: What happened when Aaron's rod became a serpent before Pharaoh?

text.en: Aaron's serpent swallowed the magicians' serpents
The magicians' rods became serpents, and one consumed Aaron's
The magicians refused to copy the sign before Pharaoh
The magicians copied the sign, then all rods became wood again

explanation.en: The Egyptian magicians also made their rods become serpents, but Aaron's rod swallowed their rods; Pharaoh still did not listen.

prompt.en: In Jesus' comparison of two builders, what made the first one wise?

text.en: He heard the teaching but chose his own response
He heard Jesus' words and obeyed them
He built on sand after searching for rock
He copied another builder's design and materials

explanation.en: Jesus compares the person who hears his words and does them to a wise builder whose house stands through storm and flood.

prompt.en: When the disciples entered a town, what did Jesus tell them to do about lodging?

text.en: Stay with the town's wealthiest household
Move each night to meet more families
Find a worthy household and remain there
Sleep outside until the whole town welcomed them

explanation.en: Jesus tells them to find out who is worthy in the town or village and stay there until they leave.

prompt.en: What comparison did Jesus use to answer the question about healing on the Sabbath?

text.en: A farmer gathering grain before sunset
A priest offering a sacrifice at the temple
A shepherd lifting a sheep from a pit
A traveler resting after a long journey

explanation.en: Jesus asks whether someone would rescue a sheep from a pit on the Sabbath, then says a person is worth more and it is lawful to do good.

prompt.en: Why did Nicodemus conclude that Jesus was a teacher who came from God?

text.en: Jesus' signs convinced him God was with Jesus
The temple council had publicly appointed him
John the Baptist had sent him to Nicodemus
Jesus had studied under the Jerusalem rulers

explanation.en: Nicodemus says that no one could do the signs Jesus performed unless God were with him.

prompt.en: What obstacle did the sick man describe when Jesus asked if he wanted to be made well?

text.en: Other bathers blocked his way to the water
No helper could get him into the pool first
Attendants reserved the pool for other visitors
The water no longer stirred when he arrived

explanation.en: The man says he has no one to put him into the pool when its water is stirred, and another gets there first.

prompt.en: In Jesus' sheepfold comparison, what enables the sheep to follow their own shepherd?

text.en: They recognize his voice and follow him
They follow the person carrying food
They choose the familiar path through the gate
They wait for the gatekeeper to call them

explanation.en: Jesus says the sheep know their shepherd's voice, follow him, and flee from strangers whose voices they do not know.
